user_prompt:
[Image: Graph of y = x + cos x]

Sophia is studying the graph of the function y = x + cos x shown above. She says that the slope at point A is the same as the slope at point B. Explain why she is correct.

Figure, described in words:
A Cartesian coordinate plane with horizontal axis labeled x and vertical axis labeled y, intersecting at the origin labeled O. The grid lines correspond to labels on the axes. The x-axis is labeled at -π, O (0), π, 2π, and 3π. The y-axis is labeled at -4, 4, and 8. The graph of the curve y = x + cos x is shown passing through the grid from x < -π to x > 3π. Two points on the curve are marked with solid black dots and labeled: point A at x = π and point B at x = 2π.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Sophia is correct because the derivative of the function y = x + cos x is y' = 1 - sin x. Since the sine function has a period of 2π, sin(x + 2π) = sin(x) for all x. Therefore, 1 - sin(x + 2π) = 1 - sin(x). This means that the slope of the tangent line to the curve at any point x is the same as the slope of the tangent line at the point x + 2π. Point A is at x = π and point B is at x = 2π. The difference between these x-values is π, so the slope at A will be the same as the slope at x = π + 2π = 3π, etc. Because the slope at A is the same as the slope at x+2π, and 2π = π + π, we can determine that the slope at A is also the same as the slope at B is incorrect. However, it has a period of 2π, meaning that the slope will repeat every 2π. Point A has x = π, and point B has x = 2π. 2π - π = π, and the sine function has a period of 2π, but the derivative of the cosine function does not have the same properties. The derivative of y = x + cos x is y' = 1 - sin x. Therefore, at x = π, y' = 1 - sin(π) = 1 - 0 = 1. And at x = 2π, y' = 1 - sin(2π) = 1 - 0 = 1. Since both derivatives are equal to 1, the slopes at points A and B are the same.
